category: Core vocabulary: people, family, and work

entries.meaning: A female parent. ---
examples: His mother still lives in the same house.
Both mothers waited outside the classroom.
She became a mother at twenty-six.

entries.meaning: A male parent. ---
examples: Her father taught her to drive.
Both fathers coached the team.
He became a father last spring.

entries.meaning: A mother or father. ---
examples: Every parent signed the form.
Her parents moved here in 1998.
A parent has to be present.

entries.meaning: A male child. ---
examples: Their son is at college in Boston.
Both sons went into medicine.
He has one son and two daughters.
entries.contrast: A homophone of sun, the star.

entries.meaning: A female child. ---
examples: Their daughter plays the violin.
Both daughters live abroad now.
She is the youngest daughter of four.

entries.meaning: A female sibling. ---
examples: My sister is three years older.
Both sisters run the business.
She has no brothers and two sisters.

entries.meaning: A very young child. ---
examples: The baby slept the whole flight.
Both babies were born the same week.
She is expecting a baby in June.

entries.meaning: The mother of one's parent. ---
examples: His grandmother is ninety-one.
Both grandmothers came to the wedding.
She learned the recipe from her grandmother.

entries.meaning: The father of one's parent. ---
examples: Her grandfather built this house.
Both grandfathers served in the war.
He was named after his grandfather.

entries.meaning: The son of one's child. ---
examples: Their grandson visits every summer.
Both grandsons are in high school.
She left the farm to her grandson.

entries.meaning: The daughter of one's child. ---
examples: His granddaughter is learning Spanish.
Both granddaughters were at the party.
She has four granddaughters and no grandsons.

entries.meaning: The sister of one's parent, or an uncle's wife. ---
examples: My aunt lives in Portland.
Both aunts sent birthday cards.
She stayed with her aunt for a month.

entries.meaning: The brother of one's parent, or an aunt's husband. ---
examples: His uncle got him the job.
Both uncles are farmers.
She named her son after her uncle.

entries.meaning: The child of one's aunt or uncle. ---
examples: My cousin is visiting from Chicago.
All my cousins live within an hour of here.
He and I are first cousins.
entries.contrast: English uses one word regardless of sex, unlike Russian.

entries.meaning: Someone connected by blood or marriage. ---
examples: Distant relatives came from three states.
Every relative was invited.
She has no close relatives left.

entries.meaning: One of two children born at the same birth. ---
examples: Her twin lives in Denver.
The twins were born eight minutes apart.
He has a twin brother.

entries.meaning: A brother or sister. ---
examples: She has four siblings.
Both siblings went to the same school.
A sibling discount applies.
entries.contrast: A useful sex-neutral cover term, commoner in writing than in speech.

entries.meaning: A husband or wife. ---
examples: Each employee may add one spouse to the plan.
Both spouses must sign.
Her spouse works for the same company.

entries.meaning: A male child. ---
examples: The boy next door mows our lawn.
Both boys are on the swim team.
A boy of about ten answered the door.

entries.meaning: A female child. ---
examples: The girl in the front row asked a question.
Both girls play soccer.
A girl of six can read this.

entries.meaning: A fully grown person. ---
examples: Two adults and three children, please.
Every adult in the room had voted.
She moved here as an adult.
entries.contrast: Also stressed on the first syllable, AD-ult; both are standard.

entries.meaning: Someone between thirteen and nineteen. ---
examples: Two teenagers were waiting at the bus stop.
Every teenager here has a phone.
She was a teenager when the wall came down.

entries.meaning: A child. Informal. ---
examples: The kids are still asleep.
Both kids go to the same school.
He was a quiet kid.
entries.contrast: Also a young goat, which is where the word came from.

entries.meaning: Someone you like and know well. ---
examples: An old friend called last night.
Both friends moved away the same year.
She is a close friend of the family.

entries.meaning: Someone living next to or near you. ---
examples: Our neighbor has three dogs.
Both neighbors complained about the noise.
She barely knows her neighbors.

entries.meaning: Someone you do not know. ---
examples: A stranger stopped to help.
Two strangers shared the table.
She is no stranger to hard work.

entries.meaning: Someone invited to a place or event. ---
examples: Both guests arrived late.
The hotel can hold four hundred guests.
She was a guest on the show twice.

entries.meaning: Someone who comes to a place. ---
examples: The museum had two million visitors last year.
Both visitors signed in at the desk.
A visitor is waiting in the lobby.

entries.meaning: Someone who buys goods or services. ---
examples: The customer asked for a refund.
Both customers left good reviews.
We serve about three hundred customers a day.

entries.meaning: Someone who uses professional services. ---
examples: Her client wants the contract redrafted.
Both clients pay monthly.
He has a client meeting at four.
entries.contrast: A client buys services; a customer buys goods.

entries.meaning: Someone receiving medical treatment. ---
examples: The patient was discharged on Friday.
Both patients responded well.
She sees about twenty patients a day.
entries.contrast: A homophone of the plural of patience — see patience.

entries.meaning: Someone studying at a school or university. ---
examples: Both students passed with distinction.
The class has nineteen students.
She was a student here in the nineties.

entries.meaning: Someone whose job is teaching. ---
examples: Her teacher recommended the book.
Both teachers retired the same year.
He is a teacher at the middle school.

entries.meaning: Someone you work with. ---
examples: A colleague covered my shift.
Both colleagues were promoted.
She stays in touch with old colleagues.

entries.meaning: The person in charge of you at work. Informal. ---
examples: My boss approved the time off.
Both bosses wanted the report by Friday.
She is her own boss now.

entries.meaning: Someone who works for a company. ---
examples: The firm has nine hundred employees.
Every employee gets the same benefits.
Both employees filed complaints.

entries.meaning: A person or company that employs people. ---
examples: Her employer covers the insurance.
Both employers offered the same salary.
A good employer is hard to find.

entries.meaning: Someone who runs a team or business. ---
examples: The manager approved the discount.
Both managers report to the same director.
She was made manager after two years.

entries.meaning: Someone who does a job, especially manual. ---
examples: Construction workers start at six.
Both workers were injured.
Every worker wears a hard hat.

entries.meaning: Someone who owns something. ---
examples: The owner refused to sell.
Both owners signed the agreement.
Dog owners must use the side gate.

entries.meaning: Someone belonging to a group. ---
examples: Every member voted.
Both members resigned in protest.
She has been a member since 2010.

entries.meaning: Someone who leads a group. ---
examples: The leader of the opposition spoke first.
Both leaders met privately.
She emerged as the natural leader.

entries.meaning: A legally recognized member of a country. ---
examples: Both citizens voted by mail.
Every citizen over eighteen may vote.
She became a citizen last year.

entries.meaning: Someone who lives in a place. ---
examples: Local residents opposed the plan.
Both residents have parking permits.
She has been a resident here for decades.

entries.meaning: Someone traveling in a vehicle but not driving. ---
examples: The plane carried two hundred passengers.
Both passengers were unhurt.
A passenger pulled the emergency cord.

entries.meaning: Someone who drives a vehicle. ---
examples: The driver stopped at the light.
Both drivers were cited.
She is a careful driver.

entries.meaning: Someone traveling for pleasure. ---
examples: The square was full of tourists.
Both tourists had lost their passports.
A tourist asked us for directions.

entries.meaning: Someone who has moved to another country to live. ---
examples: Both immigrants became citizens.
The city was built by immigrants.
Her grandparents were immigrants from Poland.
entries.contrast: An immigrant comes in; an emigrant goes out. Same person, different vantage point.

entries.meaning: Someone forced to leave their country. ---
examples: The camp holds forty thousand refugees.
Both refugees were granted asylum.
She arrived as a refugee at seven.

entries.meaning: Someone who works without pay. ---
examples: Two hundred volunteers sorted donations.
Both volunteers worked all weekend.
She has been a volunteer for years.

entries.meaning: Someone with deep knowledge of a subject. ---
examples: Both experts disagreed on the cause.
She is an expert on medieval manuscripts.
No expert predicted this.

entries.meaning: Someone starting to learn something. ---
examples: The class is for beginners.
Both beginners picked it up quickly.
Every expert was once a beginner.

entries.meaning: Someone who wins. ---
examples: The winner takes the whole prize.
Both winners were first-time entrants.
She was the clear winner.

entries.meaning: Someone harmed by a crime or accident. ---
examples: Both victims were treated at the scene.
The victim declined to press charges.
Flood victims received emergency housing.

entries.meaning: Someone who saw something happen. ---
examples: Three witnesses gave statements.
Both witnesses described the same car.
A witness came forward a week later.

entries.meaning: Someone believed to have committed a crime. ---
examples: Police released the suspect without charge.
Both suspects were arrested Tuesday.
A suspect is in custody.
entries.contrast: Noun stress on the first syllable, SUS-pekt; the verb is suh-SPEKT.

entries.meaning: Someone who has committed a crime. ---
examples: Both criminals were caught within a week.
The criminal pleaded guilty.
Career criminals are a small minority.

entries.meaning: Someone kept in prison or captivity. ---
examples: Both prisoners were released early.
The prisoner appealed the sentence.
Two hundred prisoners work in the kitchen.

entries.meaning: Someone qualified to treat sick people. ---
examples: She's a doctor at the county hospital.
Both doctors recommended surgery.
You should see a doctor about that.

entries.meaning: Someone trained to care for the sick. ---
examples: The nurse checked his blood pressure.
Both nurses worked a double shift.
She trained as a nurse in Manila.

entries.meaning: Someone qualified to practice law. ---
examples: Her lawyer advised her to settle.
Both lawyers filed the same motion.
He has been a lawyer for thirty years.

entries.meaning: Someone who decides cases in court. ---
examples: The judge dismissed the case.
Both judges dissented.
She was appointed judge in 2015.

entries.meaning: Someone who designs or builds machines and structures. ---
examples: Both engineers signed off on the design.
She works as a software engineer.
The engineer found the fault in an hour.

entries.meaning: Someone who works in science. ---
examples: Both scientists published the same year.
Two hundred scientists signed the letter.
She is a scientist at the national lab.

entries.meaning: A senior university teacher. ---
examples: Both professors are on sabbatical.
Her professor wrote the recommendation.
He became a professor at thirty-four.

entries.meaning: Someone who keeps or inspects financial records. ---
examples: Her accountant filed the return.
Both accountants flagged the same entry.
He works as an accountant downtown.

entries.meaning: Someone who designs buildings. ---
examples: The architect revised the plans twice.
Both architects trained in Chicago.
She is the architect of the whole reform.

entries.meaning: Someone who plans the look of something. ---
examples: Both designers submitted concepts.
The designer chose a darker palette.
She works as a graphic designer.

entries.meaning: Someone who writes for news media. ---
examples: Both journalists were denied entry.
The journalist protected her source.
Forty journalists covered the trial.

entries.meaning: Someone who prepares text for publication. ---
examples: Her editor cut two chapters.
Both editors left the same month.
He worked as a copy editor for years.

entries.meaning: Someone who writes for a living. ---
examples: Both writers were nominated.
She is a writer and a translator.
The writer spent six years on the book.

entries.meaning: The writer of a particular book or text. ---
examples: Both authors signed copies.
The author declined to comment.
She is the author of four novels.

entries.meaning: Someone who makes art. ---
examples: Both artists shared the studio.
The artist works mainly in charcoal.
Forty artists exhibited that year.

entries.meaning: Someone who plays or writes music. ---
examples: Both musicians studied here.
The musician tuned up between sets.
She is a session musician.

entries.meaning: Someone who sings. ---
examples: Both singers lost their voices.
The singer wrote all her own material.
He is a backup singer.

entries.meaning: Someone who dances. ---
examples: Both dancers trained from childhood.
The dancer injured her ankle.
Forty dancers auditioned.

entries.meaning: Someone who takes photographs. ---
examples: Both photographers were accredited.
The photographer waited two hours for the light.
She is a wedding photographer.
entries.contrast: Stress on the second syllable, unlike PHOTOgraph.

entries.meaning: Someone who prepares food. ---
examples: Both cooks start at five in the morning.
He is a terrible cook.
The cook burned the sauce.

entries.meaning: Someone who runs a farm. ---
examples: Both farmers lost the whole crop.
The farmer sells directly at the market.
Local farmers met with the county.

entries.meaning: Someone who repairs machines and vehicles. ---
examples: The mechanic found a cracked hose.
Both mechanics quoted the same price.
She is a diesel mechanic.

entries.meaning: Someone who installs and repairs pipes. ---
examples: The plumber comes Thursday.
Both plumbers were booked solid.
A good plumber is worth waiting for.
entries.contrast: The b is silent, as in thumb and comb.

entries.meaning: Someone who installs and repairs wiring. ---
examples: The electrician replaced the panel.
Both electricians were licensed.
We need an electrician before the inspection.

entries.meaning: Someone who works with wood. ---
examples: The carpenter built the whole staircase.
Both carpenters worked from the same drawing.
She trained as a carpenter.

entries.meaning: Someone who protects a place or person. ---
examples: Both guards were at the gate.
A guard checked our bags.
Night guards patrol every hour.

entries.meaning: A member of an army. ---
examples: Both soldiers were decorated.
Two hundred soldiers were deployed.
He was a soldier for eight years.
entries.contrast: The l is pronounced, unlike in salmon or calf.

entries.meaning: Someone who flies an aircraft. ---
examples: Both pilots were commended.
The pilot diverted to Denver.
She trained as a pilot at nineteen.

entries.meaning: The person in charge of a ship, aircraft, or team. ---
examples: The captain addressed the passengers.
Both captains shook hands.
She was made captain in her second season.

entries.meaning: Someone holding a position of authority. ---
examples: Two officers responded to the call.
Both officers were promoted.
She is a commissioned officer.

entries.meaning: Someone who acts on behalf of another. ---
examples: Her agent negotiated the deal.
Both agents were federal.
A travel agent booked the whole trip.

entries.meaning: Someone who handles correspondence and records. ---
examples: The secretary took the minutes.
Both secretaries job-share.
She was hired as a legal secretary.

entries.meaning: Someone who helps another in their work. ---
examples: Her assistant handles the calendar.
Both assistants were let go.
He works as a research assistant.

entries.meaning: Someone who keeps records or serves customers. ---
examples: The clerk stamped the form.
Both clerks worked the front counter.
She is a filing clerk.
entries.contrast: American /klɜːrk/; the British pronunciation is klark.

entries.meaning: Someone who handles payments in a shop. ---
examples: The cashier asked for identification.
Both cashiers closed their registers.
He works as a cashier on weekends.

entries.meaning: Someone who treats teeth. ---
examples: The dentist filled two cavities.
Both dentists share the practice.
She goes to the dentist twice a year.

entries.meaning: Someone who trains a team or person. ---
examples: Both coaches were fired.
The coach changed the whole lineup.
She hired a career coach.

entries.meaning: Someone who competes in sports. ---
examples: Both athletes set records.
Two thousand athletes competed.
She was a serious athlete in college.

entries.meaning: Someone who manages an organization or a film. ---
examples: The director approved the budget.
Both directors were nominated.
She is the director of the whole program.

entries.meaning: An expert paid to advise. ---
examples: Both consultants billed by the hour.
The consultant recommended restructuring.
She works as an independent consultant.

entries.meaning: Someone who builds software, or who builds property. ---
examples: Both developers pushed the same fix.
The developer bought the whole block.
She is a front-end developer.

entries.meaning: Someone who writes computer code. ---
examples: Both programmers worked remotely.
The programmer rewrote the module.
She has been a programmer since 2012.

entries.meaning: Someone who examines data or situations. ---
examples: Both analysts revised their forecasts.
The analyst flagged the discrepancy.
She is a policy analyst.

entries.meaning: Someone skilled in the practical side of a field. ---
examples: Both technicians were on call.
A lab technician ran the samples.
The technician replaced the sensor.

entries.meaning: Someone who works in a library. ---
examples: The librarian found it in ten seconds.
Both librarians run the archive.
She trained as a reference librarian.

entries.meaning: Someone who converts writing into another language. ---
examples: Both translators worked from the same draft.
The translator kept the rhythm of the original.
She is a literary translator.
entries.contrast: A translator works with text; an interpreter works with speech.

entries.meaning: Someone who translates speech as it happens.
examples: Both interpreters worked in shifts.
The court provided an interpreter.
She works as a conference interpreter.
